Invalid JSON is caught and treated as an empty body.

terms.meaning: The record's parcel numbers do not match the case's numbers.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and runtime setting
sections.what: Loads the response helper, the case service, and the official record service, and sets the Node.js runtime.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: List imported records handler
sections.what: Returns the records already imported for the case, or a not-found response if the case does not exist.
sections.why: Lets the case page show what has been imported.
sections.watch_out: The not-found message is different from the one used on other routes, so do not assume a single shared text.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Import record handler
sections.what: Reads the record id, performs the import, and returns the result. It returns 400 for a missing id, 404 when nothing matches, and 409 when the parcel identity does not match.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates bad input, a missing target, and a mismatch so the user can see the reason.
sections.watch_out: The 409 response body is the result object itself, not a wrapped error.

summary: Web address to list a case's imported official records and to import one synthetic record into the case.
purpose: Lets a case pull in one matching official-style record.
why: Likely reason: imports happen only when someone asks, so the case stays in control of what it uses.
how: GET checks the case exists and returns its records. POST reads the record id, returns 400 if it is missing or not text, calls the import service, returns 404 if the case or record is unknown, returns 409 if the parcel identity does not match, and otherwise returns the import result.
inputs: Case id in the address. POST body with an officialRecordId text field.
outputs: A list of records on GET. On POST, the import result, or errors with codes INVALID_IMPORT, NOT_FOUND, or a 409 response carrying the mismatch result.
risks: POST checks only the type of the id, not a full schema. A 409 returns the whole result object rather than a standard error wrapper, so callers must read it differently.
debug: A 409 means the parcel identity does not match the case. A 404 means the case or record is unknown. A 400 means the body is wrong.
